column7: The Secretariat-General of the Government has started the development of the first National Open Data Strategy. We are now in the analysis and pre-consultation phase, also working on an initial draft with a series of institutions (https://data.gov.ro/pages/cadrul-strategic; https://data.gov.ro/blog/rezumatul-intalnirii-prima-strategie-nationala-privind-datele-deschise).

column2:
Is there an open data policy/strategy at regional or local level?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) provide the URL and (2) title of the document(s) and (3) briefly describe.
column4: (Review 1: Answer revised to yes) Timisoara OGP Local Action Plan includes a commitment on open data: https://www.opengovpartnership.org/members/timisoara-romania/commitments/ROTMR0003/.  The commitment is aimed at increasing the quality and quantity of available open data. Proposed actions include peer exchanges, census of public data held by public institutions and other relevant stakeholders, publication of 10 high value open data sets and standardization of their structure, guidelines for periodic identification of high value data, publication and maintenance of the published data, engage re-users etc.

If yes, please briefly describe the main measures described by the action plan.
column7: The legal framework for the development of any national and sectorial strategy mandates that the strategy must have an action plan with the respective actions, milestones, responsibile institutions and monitoring indicators in place. As such, along with the development of the strategy we are also working on the Action Plan, starting from the main pillars (objectives) of the Strategy.

column2:
Does the national strategy/policy outline measures to incentivise the publication of and access to real-time or dynamic data?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the measures.
column4:
The Law transposing the Open Data Directive includes provisions on the obligation to publish real-time data. 
Review 1 - Clarification: the Law does not go in detail: art.8 (6) Public entities shall make the dynamic data they hold available to potential users for re-use, immediately after collection, through appropriate APIs and, where appropriate, by mass download. 
The implementing norms will go into further detail.
column7: More detailed provisions are included in the draft secondary legislation and further actions will be included in the Strategy under the ”HVDs Publication and Improved Data Quality” pillar/Strategic Objective

column2:

column2:
Does the national strategy/policy outline measures to support the reuse of open data by the public sector?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the measures.
column4: (Review 1: Answer revised to yes) The law includes measures to ensure data requests are processed correctly (including sanctions on non abiding institutions), data is published in open formats with metadata and using open standards, it also recommends the CC licences for published data. In addition, the aplication norms, now under development, focus on the importance of maintaining a permanent dialogue with re-users, especially in prioritising data sets for publication, to align to their needs in terms of frequency, format, availability etc.
column7:
The Strategy under development will include actions to foster the development of business models for the re-use of open data by the public sector (under the Encouraging Open Data Re-use pillar/Strategic Objective).
In addition, the Ministry for Research, Innovation and Digitalization, the Authority for the Digitalization of Romania and the Secretariat-General of the Government have initiated the approval through Government Memorandum of a document on Guidelines for the digitialisation of public services that includes recommendations for public authorities to re-use availble open data in the design and implementation of their new/re-designed digital services. The Memorandum is pending approval in the government meeting.

column4: The law includes clear measures for data requests, redress cases and the implementing act (under consultation) includes provisions on prioritisation of publication and collaboration with re-users, so as to reflect their needs.
column7: More detailed provisions are included in the draft secondary legislation and further actions will be included in the Strategy under the Encouraging Open Data Re-use pillar/Strategic Objective (https://data.gov.ro/uploads/page_images/2024-06-07-105250.761843Strategie-date-deschisepropuneri-directii-strategice29mai24.docx; https://data.gov.ro/pages/cadrul-strategic)

column2: 1.2 Governance of open data

Is there a governance structure in place that enables the participation and/or inclusion of various open data stakeholders? 

For Explanation:
*  If yes, please briefly describe the governance structure and its operating model
column4: new question
column7:
The governance structure is composed of the team within the Secretariat-General of the Government (that holds most attributions in the coordination of the open data inititative) and the Authority for the Digitalization of Romania (transposition mainly attributions).  The SGG activities are conducted with the participation /inclusion of stakeholders (data stewards from the central/local administration, re-users, academia, civil society), as reflected in the implementation of the open data commitments in the OGP National Action Plans developed, implemented and monitored in collaboration with civil society) or the active participation of stakeholders in open data meetings and debates on various issues (https://data.gov.ro/blog).
In addition to the previous arrangements, this year there have been established two new data governance bodies: 
- a National Coordination Committee on data, digital services and AI (bringing together the institutions with attributions on govt data);
- a technical group of the Committee for e-government and red tape reduction on the ”Development of a Data-Driven Public Sector” - the working groups of this Committee also work with stakeholders from outside government (civil society etc), according to its functioning regulations.

column2:
How would you classify the model used for governing open data in your country? 

For Explanation:
*  Please briefly explain why this model was chosen/works best for your country
column4: The approach is mainly top-down in terms of legislative framework, dissemination of knowledge and good practices, coordination etc. However, as there are starting to be local open data initiatives, we are now supporting them from the central level, and they are also working together to promote their good practices to peers from other municipalities.

column2:

Any local initiatives that have focused on open data have also been supported and promoted by the SGG (Timișoara: https://data.gov.ro/blog/planul-local-de-actiune-ogp-2022-2024-timisoara; Alba Iulia - ongoing talks with the representatives of developers, civil society and city hall to promote open data at local level - event in June 2024)

column2:
Is there a regular exchange of knowledge or experiences between the national open data team and the team maintaining the national portal? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe how this exchange takes place and provide evidence supporting your answer (e.g. meeting agendas, URLs to news items).
column4: The teams are part of the same office (Secretariat General of the Government), working in collaboration with the Authority for the Digitalisation of Romania that transposes the EU legislation in the field. The collaboration is permanent.  the national open data team is the composed of the Secretariat General of the Government, that manages the national portal but also has broader coordination attributions and contributes to the legislative process on open data, and the Authority for the Digitalisation of Romania, that is in charge mainly with transposing EU legislation and limited open data attributions otherwise. The collaboration is constant but it is mainly on an inter-institutional level (online, offline, official and informal communication). For example, the law transposing the Directive was initiated and developed by both ADR and SGG. It also translates in partnership between the SGG and ADR in organising public meetings and debates (ex. https://data.gov.ro/blog/grup-de-lucru-date-deschise-pna-2022-2024) or in project implementation (ex. OECD Digital Government Review, including open data: https://sgg.gov.ro/1/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/PNP-003-anunt-website.pdf)

column2:
Does the governance model include the appointment of official roles in civil services that are dedicated to open data (e.g. open data officers)?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please describe how this task is fulfilled at public body level.
column4: Law 179/2022 states that each public entity should have an appointed data officer. Each ministry has an appointed data steward (permanently updated) and we are in a continuous process of extending this to all agencies from the central level. While the responsibilities of the data steward were imposed from the top, it was upon each ministry to decide on who to appoint, due to the differences in their internal procedures. The role of the data steward /dedicated department is further detailed in the implementing act of the Law 179/2022 (under consultation).

column2: 1.3 Open data implementation

Do data publication plans exist at public body level?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide the URL and briefly highlight the key aspects covered.
column4: Some public bodies do have data publication plans, although this is not true for all (ex.https://data.gov.ro/dataset/inventar-seturi-date-deschise-mdlpa-aprilie-2023; https://data.gov.ro/dataset/planul-de-publicare-a-datelor-deschise-consiliul-judetean-tulcea-2023). The law does require for all entities to have such publication plans.
column7: The draft secondary legislation offers a standardised template for the publication plans, and once adopted, we will also be able to monitor compliance with these plans.

column2:
What are the top 3 challenges that your country is facing in the implementation of the mentioned open data policies/strategy?

For Explanation:
* Please briefly describe.
column4: lack of allocated resources (both human and financial), lack of standardisation in the collection and managament of data, lack of coherent data governance (including at public sector body level).

column2:
Are there activities in place to address these challenges in your country (e.g. with specific national/regional/local plans or initiatives)?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the measures that you have adopted or plan to adopt to address these challenges. 
* If no, please specifiy what is hampering finding a strategic approach to solve these challenges.
column4: There are activities at national level that address these issues, including the implementation of new legislation on interoperability and government cloud, improved focus on developing digital skills (and open data knowledge in particular), requirements for the open by design for new IT systems  etc.
column7: Adding to the activities already mentioned, there are also provisions on the draft secondary legislation to ensure better resource allocation and improved data governance at institutional level (roles/workflows etc.).
